title: Sliding Window
summary: Maintain a summary of a contiguous range as it grows and shrinks, instead of recomputing every subarray.
lesson:
How it works
- A window is a contiguous range `[left, right]` that you extend on the right and shrink on the left.
- Keep a summary of the window, such as a sum, a count map, a best-so-far value, or a deque, and update it in `O(1)` amortized time per move.
- Each index enters and leaves the window at most once, so the total work is `O(n)`.

When to reach for it
- The question asks about contiguous subarrays or substrings: longest, shortest, maximum, or count.
- A brute force would examine every start and end pair in `O(n^2)` or worse.
- The window size is fixed, or a condition tells you exactly when to shrink.

Common patterns
- Fixed-size window: add the new right element and remove the element that falls off the left.
- Variable-size window: grow until the condition breaks, then shrink until it holds again.
- Running best: track the best value seen so far as the window's left edge.
- Monotonic deque: keep candidates in order so the window maximum or minimum is always at the front.

Pitfalls
- Removing the outgoing element from the summary before or after the wrong step.
- Windows with negative numbers: shrink-when-too-big logic assumes adding elements only increases the sum.
- Updating the answer at the wrong moment, either before the window is valid or after it shrinks.
